author: OpenAxolotl maintainer (concept and Meshy generation), brought inside its budget in-repo by the project's headless Blender pipeline
tool: Meshy (image-to-3D), run by the maintainer OUTSIDE this repository, then reduced inside it by tools/decimate_model.py (headless Blender 4.0.2): the Draco-compressed export was decoded, coincident vertices welded, 1,985,600 triangles collapse-decimated to 10,000, the three 2048 maps kept at their source resolution -- the texture ceiling is applied by halving, and they already sat on it, and the result gated on two-way surface deviation and on open edges. The maps were renamed by the Principled BSDF input each one feeds, so Godot's extracted textures land on contract-conforming names.
prompt: Generated by the maintainer in Meshy; the exact Meshy prompt is theirs and is not recorded in this repository. The dense source is kept at reference/coral_cove/Dredger_Rustbreaker.glb so the reduction can be re-run at any ratio. SUPERSEDES the procedurally generated Dredger from tools/blender/make_drift_fleet.py, whose provenance described it as 'a faceless dredging barge: a boxy hull over a toothed cutting drum, with an amber warning stripe on the cab'; that generator remains in the repository, still produces a valid prop, and still supplies the Flagship and the Runoff Drone, but it is no longer what ships for this unit. Shipped at the prop category's 10,000-triangle budget. A first attempt at 5,000 with 1024 maps, to fit a then-150,000-triangle whole-scene budget, was rejected on the evidence: rendered at that count this machine had lost its hose runs and railings, and the halved maps flattened the panel weathering that carries most of its look. The scene ceiling was the number that moved. Checked by render at the shipped count: red and white cab, amber warning stripe, hose runs, railings and cutting drum all read.
licenseTerms: Meshy's terms of service govern the generated mesh and its maps; the maintainer generated the asset under their own Meshy account and contributed it to this repository. The in-repo Blender pass that reduces it is Apache-2.0 with the rest of the project, but it does not change the terms on the geometry it transforms. REVIEW NEEDED (REQ-021) before any redistribution that assumes a uniform Apache-2.0 grant over assets/, and it is sharper for this asset than for the hero: the project's promise to contributors is 'build your level out of our assets', which is a grant that cannot be made over geometry whose terms are someone else's.
